title: USCIS Confirms FY2027 H-1B Cap Reached, Rules Out Second Lottery
excerpt: With 211,600 registrations — down sharply from 336,153 the prior year — the agency says it received enough petitions to fill all 85,000 slots, closing the door on unselected applicants until March 2027.
body:
• USCIS announced on July 17 that it received enough H-1B petitions to fill both the 65,000 regular cap and 20,000 master's cap for FY2027, ruling out a second lottery.
  • Unique registrations dropped to approximately 211,600, down 37% from 336,153 in the FY2026 cycle, reflecting the impact of new wage-level-weighted selection rules.
  • Unselected registrants have no path to an H-1B cap petition this fiscal year; the next opportunity is the March 2027 registration for FY2028.
  • F-1 students on OPT or STEM OPT whose work authorization expires before October 2027 face an immediate need to evaluate alternative visa strategies.

U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services confirmed that the H-1B visa cap for fiscal year 2027 has been reached, closing the door on any possibility of a second lottery for this cycle. The announcement, made on July 17, means unselected applicants must wait until March 2027 to try again.

The Numbers

USCIS received approximately 211,600 unique beneficiary registrations for the FY2027 lottery conducted in March 2026. That figure represents a steep 37% decline from the 336,153 registrations submitted for FY2026, a drop that immigration attorneys attribute in part to new wage-level-weighted selection rules that favor higher-paid positions.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8b_OyU8rOFI

The congressionally mandated cap comprises 65,000 regular H-1B visas and 20,000 additional slots reserved for applicants with U.S. advanced degrees, commonly known as the master's cap. Employers had until June 30, 2026 to submit full petitions for selected beneficiaries. USCIS determined that the petition volume was sufficient to fill both allocations without additional selections.

No Second Chance This Year

In prior years, USCIS occasionally conducted second-round lottery selections when initial filings did not produce enough approvable petitions to use all available cap numbers. For FY2027, the agency has confirmed that no additional selections will take place.

"Registrations that were not selected for FY2027 should no longer be expected to receive a second-round selection for this cap season."

— Murthy Law Firm

Employers have begun receiving non-selection notices in their USCIS online accounts. For many foreign nationals, the announcement triggers an immediate reassessment of immigration strategy. The next opportunity to file a cap-subject H-1B petition will be through the March 2027 registration for FY2028, with the earliest potential start date of October 1, 2027.

Impact on OPT and STEM OPT Workers

The cap announcement carries particular urgency for foreign nationals in F-1 student status working under Optional Practical Training or STEM OPT extensions. Those whose employment authorization expires before October 2027 face a gap with no cap-subject H-1B path available in the interim.

Immigration attorneys are advising affected workers and their employers to evaluate alternatives, including O-1 visas for individuals with extraordinary ability, L-1 intracompany transfers, or employer-sponsored green card processes that can provide work authorization through concurrent filing.

The Wage-Weighted Shift

The FY2027 cycle was the first conducted under USCIS's new wage-level-weighted selection process, which gives higher priority to registrations offering higher compensation. The system was designed to reduce speculative filings by staffing companies and ensure H-1B slots go to positions offering competitive wages.

The 37% decline in total registrations suggests the new rules had a measurable dampening effect. Whether the drop reflects reduced gaming of the system, employer caution about the new rules, or broader hiring slowdowns in the tech sector remains an open question heading into the next cycle.

What Employers Should Do Now

For companies with key employees who were not selected, immigration counsel recommends several steps: review current visa status and expiration dates, assess eligibility for alternative work visa categories, and begin PERM labor certification processes where applicable. Employers sponsoring workers for cap-subject H-1B petitions should also start planning early for the FY2028 registration window, which is expected to open in early March 2027.

The cap announcement marks the definitive close of this year's H-1B season and shifts the conversation from lottery odds to long-term immigration planning — a transition that affects hundreds of thousands of workers, employers, and families across the United States.
